To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the risk of new-onset ST abnormalities is increased in men with metabolic syndrome (MS).
a modified NCEP definition of MS predicts ST-T abnormalities, and that WBC count adds to the risk prediction of new-onset ST abnormalities and type 1 diabetes in Japanese men.

the risk of developing isolated ST-T abnormalities was increased with increasing number of metabolic syndrome components, and that the presence of the metabolic syndrome was a stronger risk factor for type 2 diabetic than for non-diabetic subjects.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the metabolic syndrome (defined by a modified National Cholesterolemia Education Program (NCP) criteria) and the risk of developing isolated ST-T abnormalities (a sub-clinical manifestation of coronary artery disease) and type 2 diabates.
the metabolic syndrome (defined by the National Cholesterol Education Panel) and its association with new-onset ST-segment-T-wave (ST-T) abnormalities and type 1 and type 2 diabetics in Japanese men.
the relationship between the MS and the risk of developing new-onset ST-segment-T wave abnormalities and type 1 diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the MS and WBC count are independent risk factors for the development of ST-T abnormalities and/or type 2 diabetes.
the metabolic syndrome predicts the risk of ST-T abnormalities and the risk of type II diabetes.
the MS is a strong predictor for new-onset ST abnormalities and type 1 diabetes in Japanese men, and that the WBC count is a strong predictor of new-onset ST abnormality in Japanese men.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of a metabolic syndrome is associated with a higher incidence of new-onset ST-segment/T-wave changes, and that this association is stronger in men who have higher WBC counts.
WBC count is a strong independent predictor for ST-T abnormalities as well as type 2 diabetes.
WBC count is an independent risk factor for ST-T abnormalities in men with the MS. (C) 2004 by the American Diabetes Association.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MS is a powerful and independent predictor of ST-T abnormalities and diabetes in Japanese men.
the NCEP-ATP III definition of metabolic syndrome is a strong predictor for ST-T abnormalities as well as type 2 diabetes.
a modified NCEP definition predicts new onset of ST-T abnormalities and diabetes.
